2026-08-04T11:32:08.3911581Z [36;1m## Formatting Guidelines[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3912062Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3912778Z [36;1m- Lead with the most important information — your first sentence should be the key takeaway[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3913732Z [36;1m- Be concise and actionable — no filler or praise[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3914591Z [36;1m- Use `<details>` and `<summary>` tags for long sections to keep responses scannable[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3915700Z [36;1m- Wrap branch names and @-references in backticks to avoid pinging users[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3916703Z [36;1m- Include code snippets with file paths and line numbers when referencing the codebase[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3917812Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3918187Z [36;1m## Rigor[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3918584Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3919403Z [36;1m**Silence is better than noise. A false positive wastes a human's time and erodes trust in every future report.**[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3920325Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3921201Z [36;1m- If you claim something is missing or broken, show the exact evidence in the code — file path, line number, and what you observed.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3922730Z [36;1m- If a conclusion depends on assumptions you haven't confirmed, do not assert it. Verify first; if you cannot verify, do not report.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3924057Z [36;1m- "I don't know" is better than a wrong answer. `noop` is better than a speculative finding.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3925159Z [36;1m- It's worth the time to verify now versus guessing and forcing someone else to verify later.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3927211Z [36;1m- Before filing any issue or opening any PR, re-read your own output as a skeptical reviewer. Ask: "Would a senior engineer on this team find this useful, or would they close it immediately?" If the answer is "close," call `noop` instead.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3929488Z [36;1m- Only report findings you would confidently defend in a code review. If you feel the need to hedge with "might," "could," or "possibly," the finding is not ready to file.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3930727Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3931117Z [36;1m## MCP Pagination[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3931565Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3932879Z [36;1mMCP tool responses have a **25,000 token limit**. When responses exceed this limit, the call fails and you must retry with pagination — wasting turns and tokens. Use proactive pagination to stay under the limit.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3934408Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3934819Z [36;1m### Recommended `perPage` Values[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3935371Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3935996Z [36;1m- **5-10**: For detailed items (PR diffs, files with patches, issues with comments)[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3937168Z [36;1m- **20-30**: For medium-detail lists (commits, review comments, issue lists)[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3938106Z [36;1m- **50-100**: For simple list operations (branches, labels, tags)[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3938756Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3939158Z [36;1m### Pagination Pattern[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3939653Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3940131Z [36;1mWhen you need all results from a paginated API:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3940722Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3941258Z [36;1m1. Fetch the first page with a conservative `perPage` value[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3942035Z [36;1m2. Process the results before fetching the next page[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3943031Z [36;1m3. Continue fetching pages until you receive fewer results than `perPage` (indicating the last page)[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3943973Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3944804Z [36;1mIf you see `MCP tool response exceeds maximum allowed tokens`, retry with a smaller `perPage` value (halve it).[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3945716Z [36;1m[0m

2026-08-04T11:32:08.3961509Z [36;1m[0m

If applicable instructions materially conflict and the conflict cannot be resolved from authoritative context, do not guess.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3989463Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3993449Z [36;1mBefore deciding to create content, search the checked-out repository and published docs for existing canonical coverage. Prefer updating the canonical page over creating a duplicate. Determine whether the visible documentation is generated, federated, or sourced from another repository or specification, and edit only the true source. If the required source, navigation, redirect, or configuration file is protected by the safe-output policy, classify the issue as out of scope instead of editing rendered output or omitting a required companion change.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.3997110Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4000220Z [36;1mFor substantive drafting, classify the intended content as an Elastic overview, how-to, tutorial, troubleshooting page, or changelog before writing. Use the installed `docs-content-type-checker` in classify mode and fetch the current guidance for the selected type through the Elastic Docs MCP server. If no type fits cleanly, check whether the change belongs as a section of an existing page. For a small correction, preserve the existing page type and structure rather than forcing a new classification.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4003294Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4003701Z [36;1mThe issue is in scope when:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4004196Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4004922Z [36;1m- The requested documentation outcome and definition of done are clear.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4006370Z [36;1m- Relevant technical or product claims can be verified from the repository, linked implementation work, or other authoritative context supplied in the issue.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4008296Z [36;1m- The work can be completed within the configured documentation-only file, patch-size, file-count, and time guardrails.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4009298Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4011475Z [36;1mThe issue is out of scope only when essential context is missing or contradictory, required claims cannot be verified without guessing, the requested change requires protected or non-documentation files, or the work cannot fit within the configured execution guardrails. Do not infer missing product behavior or silently narrow a larger request to make it fit.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4013783Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4015353Z [36;1mFor an out-of-scope issue, use `add_comment` once with one short paragraph naming the missing, conflicting, or unverifiable context and what a human should add, use `add_labels` to add `docs-agent-declined`, then call `noop` and stop. Do not edit files.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4017176Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4018042Z [36;1mIf the issue is in scope but already resolved or does not warrant a source change, call `noop` with a concise reason and stop.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4019020Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4019439Z [36;1m## 2. Refine the structure and draft[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4019978Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4022152Z [36;1mBefore editing, use the Elastic Docs MCP server to fetch current contribution guidance and relevant published documentation. Do not rely on remembered guidance when the MCP server can provide the source. Establish the intended reader, their goal, prerequisites, expected outcome, content type, canonical page, and the smallest structure that satisfies the issue.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4024436Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4025319Z [36;1mAt minimum, fetch `/docs/contribute-docs` and the guidance page relevant to the requested content. Common references include:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4026321Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4027502Z [36;1m- Style guide: `/docs/contribute-docs/style-guide` and its relevant voice, accessibility, grammar, word-choice, formatting, or UI-writing subpage.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4029218Z [36;1m- Content types: `/docs/contribute-docs/content-types` and the relevant overview, how-to, tutorial, troubleshooting, or changelog guidance.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4031076Z [36;1m- Cumulative documentation and `applies_to`: `/docs/contribute-docs/how-to/cumulative-docs/guidelines` and `/docs/contribute-docs/how-to/cumulative-docs/reference`.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4032313Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4034815Z [36;1mUse `elastic-docs.search_docs` and `elastic-docs.find_related_docs` to locate current published coverage and useful sibling pages. Use `elastic-docs.get_document_by_url` to read candidate pages and known guidance. Use `elastic-docs.find_inconsistencies` when the issue concerns conflicting or duplicated published content. Keep searches targeted and paginate MCP results as instructed by the imported pagination guidance.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4037590Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4038108Z [36;1mUse sources according to their role:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4038646Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4039356Z [36;1m- Repository and linked implementation evidence establish technical and product behavior.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4040638Z [36;1m- Repository-local instructions establish contribution and file-layout requirements.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4041811Z [36;1m- MCP-fetched Elastic Docs Contribution guidelines establish the current authoring standard.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4043171Z [36;1m- Canonical published docs and nearby source pages establish terminology, placement, cross-links, and surrounding context.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4044181Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4045560Z [36;1mIf authoritative sources conflict on a claim essential to the draft, or the MCP server cannot provide the required guidance or published-doc context, call `report_incomplete` and stop before editing.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4047134Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4049579Z [36;1mLocate the affected documentation files and make the focused change that fully resolves the documented definition of done. Follow repository-local contribution instructions together with the MCP-fetched Elastic Docs Contribution guidelines. Make every change justified by the gathered evidence, preserve established terminology and page structure where appropriate, and do not touch unrelated files.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4052138Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4054316Z [36;1mDraft around the reader's intended outcome rather than the implementation's API or file layout. Keep one canonical explanation, link to existing background or reference material instead of repeating it, and use the lightest structure that works. Apply the selected content type's required elements and anti-patterns. Use the installed authoring skills conditionally:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4056608Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4057629Z [36;1m- `docs-applies-to-tagging` for version, deployment, availability, lifecycle, or cumulative-documentation decisions.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4059131Z [36;1m- `docs-syntax-help` for MyST Markdown or Elastic directive syntax that cannot be resolved confidently from nearby pages.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4060473Z [36;1m- `docs-frontmatter-description` when a new or changed page needs a `description` in scope.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4061313Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4062418Z [36;1mDo not broaden the patch merely to apply a skill. Do not move or rename a published page unless the required redirect can also be changed within the allowed-file policy.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4063631Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4065008Z [36;1mAfter editing, inspect the complete diff and list of changed files. If any changed path is unrelated, outside the configured documentation paths, or protected by policy, remove that change before proposing the draft.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4066494Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4067044Z [36;1m## 3. Test with a fresh reader[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4067557Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4068105Z [36;1mAfter drafting, use the `reader-tester` sub-agent with only:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4068774Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4069368Z [36;1m- The intended reader, their goal, and the expected outcome from the issue.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4070596Z [36;1m- The complete proposed content of every changed page or section, plus only the linked passages required to understand it.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4071571Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4072853Z [36;1mDo not give the reader tester your drafting rationale, implementation evidence, contribution guidelines, or other private context. The test must reveal whether the documentation stands on its own.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4074970Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4077235Z [36;1mAsk the reader tester to predict three to five realistic reader questions, answer them using only the supplied documentation, and identify blocking ambiguity, missing prerequisites, contradictions, assumed knowledge, or unclear next actions. This is a comprehension test, not a Vale, syntax, style, or technical-accuracy review.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4079355Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4082511Z [36;1mIf the reader test finds a blocking documentation gap that can be resolved from already gathered authoritative context, make a surgical correction and run the reader test once more. Stop after at most two reader-test rounds. Optional improvements do not block a draft. If a blocking gap remains because essential context is missing or unverifiable, use `add_comment` once to summarize what the reader could not determine and what context a human must add, add `docs-agent-declined`, call `noop`, and do not open a pull request.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4085632Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4086124Z [36;1m## 4. Stage a draft pull request[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4086642Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4088619Z [36;1mWhen the focused draft passes reader testing, use `create_pull_request` exactly once. Keep it a draft and do not enable auto-merge. Link the triggering issue without closing it. Do not run Vale, docs-builder validation, or a documentation review; those happen separately after the draft is created.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4090515Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4090942Z [36;1mThe pull request body must contain:[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4091479Z [36;1m[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4091915Z [36;1m- One paragraph summarizing the change.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4093086Z [36;1m- A short triage rationale explaining which issue and implementation evidence made the task sufficiently specified for autonomous handling.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4094834Z [36;1m- A `Drafting sources` section listing the contribution-guideline pages, published documentation, and linked implementation evidence consulted.[0m
2026-08-04T11:32:08.4096499Z [36;1m- A `Reader test` section listing the reader goal, number of test rounds, and whether any blocking comprehension gaps remained.[0m

2026-08-04T11:32:08.8952156Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8952446Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8952629Z To create a pull request:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8953203Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8954306Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8956167Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8958219Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8959372Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8960980Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8961880Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8964469Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8967043Z

2026-08-04T11:32:08.8998835Z ## Formatting Guidelines
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8999110Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.8999680Z - Lead with the most important information — your first sentence should be the key takeaway
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9000580Z - Be concise and actionable — no filler or praise
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9001530Z - Use `<details>` and `<summary>` tags for long sections to keep responses scannable
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9002526Z - Wrap branch names and @-references in backticks to avoid pinging users
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9003450Z - Include code snippets with file paths and line numbers when referencing the codebase
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9004038Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9004197Z ## Rigor
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9004404Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9004960Z **Silence is better than noise. A false positive wastes a human's time and erodes trust in every future report.**
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9005681Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9006407Z - If you claim something is missing or broken, show the exact evidence in the code — file path, line number, and what you observed.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9008055Z - If a conclusion depends on assumptions you haven't confirmed, do not assert it. Verify first; if you cannot verify, do not report.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9009297Z - "I don't know" is better than a wrong answer. `noop` is better than a speculative finding.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9010317Z - It's worth the time to verify now versus guessing and forcing someone else to verify later.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9012103Z - Before filing any issue or opening any PR, re-read your own output as a skeptical reviewer. Ask: "Would a senior engineer on this team find this useful, or would they close it immediately?" If the answer is "close," call `noop` instead.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9014310Z - Only report findings you would confidently defend in a code review. If you feel the need to hedge with "might," "could," or "possibly," the finding is not ready to file.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9015295Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9015479Z ## MCP Pagination
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9015716Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9017106Z MCP tool responses have a **25,000 token limit**. When responses exceed this limit, the call fails and you must retry with pagination — wasting turns and tokens. Use proactive pagination to stay under the limit.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9018334Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9018535Z ### Recommended `perPage` Values
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9018861Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9019249Z - **5-10**: For detailed items (PR diffs, files with patches, issues with comments)
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9020139Z - **20-30**: For medium-detail lists (commits, review comments, issue lists)
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9020932Z - **50-100**: For simple list operations (branches, labels, tags)
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9021385Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9021566Z ### Pagination Pattern
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9021833Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9022065Z When you need all results from a paginated API:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9022456Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9022739Z 1. Fetch the first page with a conservative `perPage` value
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9023428Z 2. Process the results before fetching the next page
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9024334Z 3. Continue fetching pages until you receive fewer results than `perPage` (indicating the last page)
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9025006Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9025557Z If you see `MCP tool response exceeds maximum allowed tokens`, retry with a smaller `perPage` value (halve it).
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9026271Z

2026-08-04T11:32:08.9036222Z - `docs-frontmatter-description`
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9036546Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9037867Z Use only the installed skills relevant to the issue. They supplement, but do not replace, current MCP-fetched guidance and repository-local instructions. Do not invoke documentation review skills or run their checks.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9039179Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9039394Z ## 1. Gather context, classify, and triage
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9039756Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9041623Z Read the complete issue and determine whether it provides enough verifiable context to implement the requested documentation work. Do not restrict eligibility by change category: corrections, new content, substantial revisions, structural changes, navigation work, examples, and other documentation maintenance are all potentially in scope.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9043608Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9045847Z Discover and inspect relevant evidence referenced by the issue or its comments, including linked code pull requests, commits, documentation pull requests, specifications, and related issues. For a linked pull request, use read-only `gh` commands to inspect its description, changed files, and diff. Reconcile the issue request with the implementation evidence instead of treating either source as automatically correct.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9048377Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9051613Z Discover and read the repository-level and closest path-scoped `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` files that govern the candidate documentation files. Also read applicable `CONTRIBUTING.md`, docs-specific contribution guides, navigation definitions, and two to four nearby pages of the same kind. Follow both `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` when present; more narrowly scoped repository instructions take precedence over broader ones. Workflow safety constraints always take precedence. If applicable instructions materially conflict and the conflict cannot be resolved from authoritative context, do not guess.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9055024Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9058137Z Before deciding to create content, search the checked-out repository and published docs for existing canonical coverage. Prefer updating the canonical page over creating a duplicate. Determine whether the visible documentation is generated, federated, or sourced from another repository or specification, and edit only the true source. If the required source, navigation, redirect, or configuration file is protected by the safe-output policy, classify the issue as out of scope instead of editing rendered output or omitting a required companion change.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9061238Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9063895Z For substantive drafting, classify the intended content as an Elastic overview, how-to, tutorial, troubleshooting page, or changelog before writing. Use the installed `docs-content-type-checker` in classify mode and fetch the current guidance for the selected type through the Elastic Docs MCP server. If no type fits cleanly, check whether the change belongs as a section of an existing page. For a small correction, preserve the existing page type and structure rather than forcing a new classification.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9066699Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9067084Z The issue is in scope when:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9067391Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9067746Z - The requested documentation outcome and definition of done are clear.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9069076Z - Relevant technical or product claims can be verified from the repository, linked implementation work, or other authoritative context supplied in the issue.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9070671Z - The work can be completed within the configured documentation-only file, patch-size, file-count, and time guardrails.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9071440Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9073462Z The issue is out of scope only when essential context is missing or contradictory, required claims cannot be verified without guessing, the requested change requires protected or non-documentation files, or the work cannot fit within the configured execution guardrails. Do not infer missing product behavior or silently narrow a larger request to make it fit.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9075604Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9077103Z For an out-of-scope issue, use `add_comment` once with one short paragraph naming the missing, conflicting, or unverifiable context and what a human should add, use `add_labels` to add `docs-agent-declined`, then call `noop` and stop. Do not edit files.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9078564Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9079172Z If the issue is in scope but already resolved or does not warrant a source change, call `noop` with a concise reason and stop.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9079948Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9080142Z ## 2. Refine the structure and draft
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9080474Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9082391Z Before editing, use the Elastic Docs MCP server to fetch current contribution guidance and relevant published documentation. Do not rely on remembered guidance when the MCP server can provide the source. Establish the intended reader, their goal, prerequisites, expected outcome, content type, canonical page, and the smallest structure that satisfies the issue.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9084466Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9085094Z At minimum, fetch `/docs/contribute-docs` and the guidance page relevant to the requested content. Common references include:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9085881Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9086639Z - Style guide: `/docs/contribute-docs/style-guide` and its relevant voice, accessibility, grammar, word-choice, formatting, or UI-writing subpage.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9088430Z - Content types: `/docs/contribute-docs/content-types` and the relevant overview, how-to, tutorial, troubleshooting, or changelog guidance.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9090164Z - Cumulative documentation and `applies_to`: `/docs/contribute-docs/how-to/cumulative-docs/guidelines` and `/docs/contribute-docs/how-to/cumulative-docs/reference`.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9091181Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9093449Z Use `elastic-docs.search_docs` and `elastic-docs.find_related_docs` to locate current published coverage and useful sibling pages. Use `elastic-docs.get_document_by_url` to read candidate pages and known guidance. Use `elastic-docs.find_inconsistencies` when the issue concerns conflicting or duplicated published content. Keep searches targeted and paginate MCP results as instructed by the imported pagination guidance.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9095856Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9096054Z Use sources according to their role:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9096384Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9096984Z - Repository and linked implementation evidence establish technical and product behavior.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9098079Z - Repository-local instructions establish contribution and file-layout requirements.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9099171Z - MCP-fetched Elastic Docs Contribution guidelines establish the current authoring standard.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9100877Z - Canonical published docs and nearby source pages establish terminology, placement, cross-links, and surrounding context.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9101696Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9102748Z If authoritative sources conflict on a claim essential to the draft, or the MCP server cannot provide the required guidance or published-doc context, call `report_incomplete` and stop before editing.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9103938Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9106139Z Locate the affected documentation files and make the focused change that fully resolves the documented definition of done. Follow repository-local contribution instructions together with the MCP-fetched Elastic Docs Contribution guidelines. Make every change justified by the gathered evidence, preserve established terminology and page structure where appropriate, and do not touch unrelated files.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9108654Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9110724Z Draft around the reader's intended outcome rather than the implementation's API or file layout. Keep one canonical explanation, link to existing background or reference material instead of repeating it, and use the lightest structure that works. Apply the selected content type's required elements and anti-patterns. Use the installed authoring skills conditionally:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9112917Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9113580Z - `docs-applies-to-tagging` for version, deployment, availability, lifecycle, or cumulative-documentation decisions.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9114979Z - `docs-syntax-help` for MyST Markdown or Elastic directive syntax that cannot be resolved confidently from nearby pages.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9116205Z - `docs-frontmatter-description` when a new or changed page needs a `description` in scope.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9117017Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9117875Z Do not broaden the patch merely to apply a skill. Do not move or rename a published page unless the required redirect can also be changed within the allowed-file policy.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9118884Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9120032Z After editing, inspect the complete diff and list of changed files. If any changed path is unrelated, outside the configured documentation paths, or protected by policy, remove that change before proposing the draft.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9121337Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9121534Z ## 3. Test with a fresh reader
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9121830Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9122133Z After drafting, use the `reader-tester` sub-agent with only:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9122581Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9122943Z - The intended reader, their goal, and the expected outcome from the issue.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9124078Z - The complete proposed content of every changed page or section, plus only the linked passages required to understand it.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9124856Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9125888Z Do not give the reader tester your drafting rationale, implementation evidence, contribution guidelines, or other private context. The test must reveal whether the documentation stands on its own.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9127239Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9128990Z Ask the reader tester to predict three to five realistic reader questions, answer them using only the supplied documentation, and identify blocking ambiguity, missing prerequisites, contradictions, assumed knowledge, or unclear next actions. This is a comprehension test, not a Vale, syntax, style, or technical-accuracy review.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9130888Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9134259Z If the reader test finds a blocking documentation gap that can be resolved from already gathered authoritative context, make a surgical correction and run the reader test once more. Stop after at most two reader-test rounds. Optional improvements do not block a draft. If a blocking gap remains because essential context is missing or unverifiable, use `add_comment` once to summarize what the reader could not determine and what context a human must add, add `docs-agent-declined`, call `noop`, and do not open a pull request.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9137397Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9137608Z ## 4. Stage a draft pull request
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9137950Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9142013Z When the focused draft passes reader testing, use `create_pull_request` exactly once. Keep it a draft and do not enable auto-merge. Link the triggering issue without closing it. Do not run Vale, docs-builder validation, or a documentation review; those happen separately after the draft is created.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9143778Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9143989Z The pull request body must contain:
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9144325Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9144533Z - One paragraph summarizing the change.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9145605Z - A short triage rationale explaining which issue and implementation evidence made the task sufficiently specified for autonomous handling.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9147448Z - A `Drafting sources` section listing the contribution-guideline pages, published documentation, and linked implementation evidence consulted.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9149006Z - A `Reader test` section listing the reader goal, number of test rounds, and whether any blocking comprehension gaps remained.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9149979Z - `Related to #<issue number>`.
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9150793Z - This note: `This draft PR was produced autonomously by docs-agent-experimental in experimental mode.`
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9152344Z - This CI note: `Safe-output PRs do not trigger CI by default. A maintainer must trigger the required checks manually.`
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9153085Z 
2026-08-04T11:32:08.9153871Z All safe outputs are staged in this first iteration. Produce complete, realistic staged previews; do not bypass staging or attempt direct GitHub writes.
